title: ICLR 2025 notes - inference & systems (summer 2025)
content:
Quick, messy notes from ICLR + a couple follow-up papers/blogs (for internal sync). Mostly systems + inference optimization stuff that maps to our runtime priorities.

Top-level takeaways (high level):
- KV cache management still a hot area: papers on memory compaction and eviction strategies. Important for long-context streaming use cases (private deployments).
- Attention/kernel optimization: more emphasis on hardware-aware kernels (tile sizes, fused ops) and dynamic kernel selection at runtime based on sequence length distribution.
- Quantization: PTQ + minimal calibration seems to be winning for latency-sensitive inference; still tradeoffs on hallucination/regression. Papers show ~2-4% quality delta on few-shot tasks for 4-bit vs FP16 in some settings.
- Batching vs tail latency: new schedulers that do adaptive batching (latency SLO aware) seem promising. Consider integrating into our smart routing policies.

Notes on specific papers / ideas to triage:
1) "Memory-compact KV caches for long-context LLMs" (arXiv:2504.01234)
- Idea: store compressed KV shards + lightweight index to reconstruct on demand. Uses blockwise quantization + LRU-ish warmup.
- Pros: 3-4x effective memory reduction in experiments; throughput hit small if warmup rate low.
- Cons: complexity of partial decompression; tricky with GPUs where random access is expensive.
- Relevance to Redwood: fits Private deployments (customers with long-context docs). Could be a feature flag for Dedicated pools where we trade throughput for capacity.
- Follow-up TODO: run small prototype with our KV layout (see PR linked). Ticket: JIRA-RED-1234.

2) "Adaptive kernel selection at inference time" (arXiv:2503.09876)
- Idea: micro-benchmark kernels per model/shard for different seq lengths and pick kernel dynamically. Use a small profiler at model load + periodic sampling.
- Observed: 15-30% perf win for medium seq lengths (128-1024) vs static choice.
- Implementation notes: need low overhead profiler + cache of kernel decisions per model-version + hardware id.
- Red flags: profiler jitter across noisy multi-tenant hosts; need stable perf numbers.

3) "Quant-aware activation calibration for PTQ" (lighting talk + blog)
- Short summary: small curated calibration sets (300-1000 sequences) plus 2-pass activation clipping yields robust PTQ for 4-bit LLMs.
- Actionable: could add to model onboarding checklist in model-catalog pipeline (automate calibration + quick regression tests).

4) "Adaptive batching scheduler" (poster)
- SLO-aware batching: prioritize low-latency requests, opportunistically batch background tasks (embeddings, retraining scoring).
- Simple heuristic works: maintain a fast-path queue for <= N tokens or high-priority routes, and a batching queue that collects until timeout or size threshold.
- Useful to integrate with our routing policies and per-route token-level SLOs in Console.

Conference tidbits / developer talks:
- Several teams emphasized observability tied to quality (prompt-level evals). Reinforces Redwood Optimize direction (auto-detect quality regressions post-rollout).
- Private deployment talks: KMS/HSM integration patterns and audit log recommendations - good ref for our security playbooks.

Rough experiments to run (prio ordered):
- P0: Kernel profiler prototype on a small fleet of GPU types (A100, H100, RTX6000) using a representative model (Llama2-13B-ish). Measure perf variance and build decision cache. Owner: Oliver.
- P1: Lightweight KV compression prototype (in Rust/CUDA) on a single-GPU Dedicated job; measure memory reduction vs throughput. Owner: Maya.
- P1: Add PTQ calibration step to model onboarding pipeline for top-10 catalog models; automated eval against held-out prompt sets. Owner: Priya (me).
- P2: Integrate adaptive batching policy into smart-router experiment branch: route by SLO, then into fast-path vs batch-path. Owner: Eng-sre + runtime.

Open questions / discussion:
- How do compressed KV approaches interact with prefix caching (we currently cache prefixes aggressively)? Do we need different cache eviction policies per deployment type?
- Stability of kernel selection across noisy multi-tenant hosts - does dedicated capacity reduce profiling noise sufficiently to justify complexity?
- For PTQ, what threshold of quality regression is acceptable for cost wins? Need product input.

Random notes / fragments:
- Benchmark numbers: paper A reports 3.2x memory saving with 10% throughput loss for 8k contexts (worth exploring).
- Links I pinged people on Slack: #eng-serving-runtime (thread link in Confluence page).
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-cache-experiment/pull/42 (initial impl + microbench).

Immediate next steps:
- Sync with Oliver + Maya next Tue to scope P0/P1 prototypes.
- Add PTQ calibration ticket to model-catalog backlog (include eval harness).
- Quick doc for Product: short bulleted one-pager on tradeoffs (memory vs latency vs cost) for KV compression - will draft and attach to Confluence.

"Notes to self":
- keep notes short in Confluence after prototype results.
- remember to capture SLOs for the adaptive batching experiment (p95 latency targets).

End of messy notes. Will clean and convert to internal doc after experiments produce numbers.
